```yaml
name: Test Rust uprobe and bpftrace

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test-bpftrace:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Rust toolchain
        uses: actions-rs/toolchain@v1
        with:
          toolchain: stable
          override: true

      - name: Install bpftrace
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y bpftrace

      - name: Build helloworld example
        run: cargo build --manifest-path=helloworld/Cargo.toml

      - name: Verify helloworld symbol
        run: |
          if ! nm -C target/debug/helloworld | grep -q hello; then
            echo "Symbol 'hello' not found in helloworld binary"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Build args example
        run: cargo build --manifest-path=args/Cargo.toml

      - name: Verify args symbol
        run: |
          if ! nm -C target/debug/args | grep -q hello; then
            echo "Symbol 'hello' not found in args binary"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Run args binary
        run: ./target/debug/args

      - name: Test bpftrace attach to helloworld
        run: |
          # Build path to the binary
          BINARY=$(pwd)/target/debug/helloworld
          # bpftrace script using wildcard for the mangled symbol
          BPF_SCRIPT="uprobe:${BINARY}:_ZN10helloworld5hello*:entry { printf(\"hello called\\n\"); }"
          LOG_FILE=bpftrace.log
          # Run bpftrace as root in background
          sudo bpftrace -e "$BPF_SCRIPT" > "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 &
          BPF_PID=$!
          # Give bpftrace a moment to attach
          sleep 1
          # Trigger the function
          "$BINARY"
          # Stop bpftrace
          kill $BPF_PID
          wait $BPF_PID
          # Verify output
          if ! grep -q "hello called" "$LOG_FILE"; then
            echo "bpftrace did not capture hello call"
            exit 1
          fi
```
